title: Digest-bound Approvals
objective: Commit approvals atomically against exact final bytes, explicit run state, canonical counts, policy, review, dispositions, and authorized actor.
description: Closes stale-state and TOCTOU gaps by revalidating all approval bindings under lock and publishing the decision and phase transition as one logical operation.
parallel_safe_reason: This slice commits decisions over state produced by every preceding slice and changes the central approval boundary.
must: Build every approval candidate from an explicit or uniquely resolved run.
Re-read exact final artifact bytes and all canonical governance bindings inside one protected critical section.
Verify artifact and input digests, version, review digest, profile and policy digests, finding and criterion counts, disposition and reason digests, run, and actor.
Re-evaluate actor authorization and independence at commit time.
Publish the decision and phase transition as one logical all-or-nothing operation.
Leave no decision or transition behind after stale state, tampering, mismatch, or injected write failure.
Derive canonical counts from structured collections and return REPRESENTATION_MISMATCH on divergence.
Expose stable machine code, status, and exit semantics without localized JSON keys.
Provide approval show, verify, and Linear-comment export from the same canonical digest-bound record.
acceptance: AC-08 is satisfied for explicit run selection and decision correlation.
AC-09 is satisfied for exact-byte binding, complete digest validation, atomic commit, and no partial state.
AC-12 is satisfied for canonical counts and REPRESENTATION_MISMATCH.
AC-13 is satisfied for approval-related machine codes, statuses, exit behavior, and clean JSON stdout.
Approval show and verify recompute canonical validity, while export reports version, artifact digest, input digest, and criterion count.
Tampering or staleness in any bound value prevents both decision publication and phase transition.
Two active runs cannot approve, invalidate, or count state for one another.
tests: node --test tests/lib/approvals.test.js tests/lib/ai-review-governance.test.js tests/lib/ai-run-state.test.js tests/commands/ai-plan.test.js tests/commands/ai-run-state.test.js tests/commands/cli-contract.test.js
